reason: Definition of operational resilience: prevent, adapt, respond, recover, learn, including sector-wide and third-party scope; core of the regulatory concept.

UK components of operational resilience, including impact tolerance versus lessons learned; matches the UK-first regulatory concept.

What impact tolerance means for critical services and its use by the board; part of the UK resilience framework.
What distinguishes UK-style resilience from classic continuity planning, namely learning from incidents; UK components of S2.
UK 2018 paper first on resilience, requirements sit alongside existing operational risk rules rather than replacing them; the S2 trap.
Fed building-blocks diagram placement of governance, ORM and supporting pillars; detail not covered by the S2 selector.
Resilience as outcome of effective operational risk management, not a substitute for it; the relationship and trap named in S2.

BCBS 2021 principles issued with revised ORM principles; resilience as an outcome of operational risk management, directly in S2.
Regulatory landscape of resilience: UK, US, BCBS, ECB DORA draft and MAS paper; matches the regulator coverage of S2.
